results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I built a Sultai (black-green-blue) graveyard deck around the three cards you named. It's a brew, so it isn't a proven list. It passed the legality check and was accepted.

**The plan:** Fill your graveyard early with Town Greeter, Molt Tender, Cache Grab and Dredger's Insight, and get Bringer of the Last Gift in there. Then cast Superior Spider-Man, which can enter as a copy of a creature card in any graveyard. Have him copy Bringer. Since you cast him, Bringer's enter trigger happens for 4 mana instead of 8: every player sacrifices their other creatures, then all the creature cards already in graveyards come back. That brings back your milled threats: Overlord of the Balemurk, Massacre Wurm, Marang River Regent and Craterhoof Behemoth.

**How Bringer reaches the graveyard:**
- **Mill:** The mill cards above can hit it directly.
- **Lotuslight Dancers:** It puts a black, a green and a blue card from your deck into your graveyard. Pick Bringer, Craterhoof and the River Regent.
- **Bitter Triumph:** It can discard Bringer as its extra cost.

**The finishers:**
- **Craterhoof:** It returns with haste and pumps every creature you control, including itself.
- **Massacre Wurm:** It returns at the same moment as the opponent's creatures, gives them all -2/-2, and makes them lose 2 life for each one that dies.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A Dimir looting deck (black-blue, discarding cards to fill the graveyard).
2. A straight black-green deck.
3. Taking the mill package from Golgari Roots (a black-green graveyard deck) and adding blue for Spider-Man.

I chose the third because Town Greeter is already part of that package and it fills the graveyard best. About 35% of the deck matches any one existing list.

**What to watch out for:**
- **Bringer hits both players.** It also brings back the opponent's dead creatures, and it sacrifices your own board too. Strategic Betrayal (main deck and sideboard), Scavenging Ooze and Ghost Vacuum clear their graveyard first. Massacre Wurm punishes whatever comes back.
- **Odds without counting mill:** you see a Spider-Man by turn 5 on the play 56.6% of the time. You see Bringer, Dancers or Bitter Triumph 86.1% of the time. You have both 47.7% of the time. Milling raises these numbers, and the mill cards can also put a milled Spider-Man into your hand.
- **Mana:** I used 23 lands plus 6 mana creatures. Golgari Roots averages about 21 lands, but this deck has more 5–8 mana cards.
- **Rotated cards:** Go for the Throat, Cut Down, Darkslick Shores, Llanowar Wastes and Underground River still appear in the archetype data, but they're no longer Standard-legal, so I left them out.

The sideboard is aimed at the top decks: Duress, Negate, Disdainful Stroke and Tishana's Tidebinder for the Vivi Cauldron and Azorius Control decks. Ooze and Ghost Vacuum are graveyard removal, and the extra Strategic Betrayal and Shoot the Sheriff are more creature removal.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built Temur Warp Landfall, and it's a brew. It's mostly green, with blue just for Spell Snare and red just for Full Bore.

**The plan:** Warp in a big creature cheaply, pump it with Full Bore, then play a land to double its power. Mightform Harmonizer doubles one creature's power every time a land enters. Full Bore gives +3/+2, and if that creature was cast for its warp cost, it also gets trample and haste. Some examples:
- **Germinating Wurm:** warp it for {1}{G} as a 5/5, add Full Bore and it's an 8/7 with trample and haste. If Harmonizer is out, one land doubles that to 16 power.
- **Harmonizer itself:** warp it for {2}{G} and add Full Bore for a 7/6 hasty trampler. Then your land drop doubles it.
- **Making the triggers bigger:** Traveling Chocobo and Starfield Vocalist each make land triggers happen twice. Fabled Passage, Evolving Wilds and Escape Tunnel give you a second land entering each turn. Icetill Explorer lets you play an extra land per turn and replay lands from your graveyard.

Spell Snare is a 1-mana counter that only hits spells costing exactly 2, like Floodpits Drowner, Jackal, Abrade and Dispelling Exhale. It lets you keep up protection without slowing your own development.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Temur Landfall (chosen):** I took the Landfall deck's engine (the fetch lands, Escape Tunnel, Llanowar Elves, Tifa Lockhart, Mossborn Hydra, Traveling Chocobo, Icetill Explorer and Snakeskin Veil) and built the warp and Full Bore payoffs around it.
2. **Temur Warp Tempo:** The Izzet Aggro burn package with Nova Hellkite and Red Tiger Mechan, plus Harmonizer.
3. **Simic Vocalist landfall with a red splash.**

I picked the first because Harmonizer needs lots of lands entering each turn, and the Landfall shell is the only proven package built to make that happen. Tifa and Mossborn Hydra also double their own stats on each landfall, so they stack with Harmonizer.

**Mana and odds:**
- **Lands:** 24, giving 24 green sources, 13 blue and 13 red. The eight fetch-style lands can find your one Island or one Mountain when you need it.
- **Odds:** By turn 4 on the play, you have an 89% chance to have drawn Harmonizer, Traveling Chocobo or Icetill Explorer. Full Bore shows up 53% of the time, and both together 46%.

**Things to know:**
- I ran check_deck on a version with 3 Icetill Explorer and no Vocalist. It came back with no errors or warnings, and it was 60% the same as an existing Landfall list (the limit for a brew is 65%). Then I swapped one Explorer for one Starfield Vocalist and submitted without re-checking. The submission was accepted with no warnings, and the swap should only lower that overlap.
- The deck has no removal in the main deck. You're relying on Spell Snare, Snakeskin Veil and simply killing your opponent fast. The sideboard brings in removal and answers aimed at the current top decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.

You can recast each one for {2}, and every recast from exile makes a 1/1 Ally token. The recasts are good value: The Earth King brings another 4/4 Bear, and Earth Kingdom Jailer exiles another creature, artifact or enchantment. Ouroboroid is cheap to bring back. All those creature arrivals add quest counters to Airbender Ascension, and Earth King's Lieutenant grows with each new Ally. Once Ascension has four counters, it blinks Appa at every end step, which repeats the whole cycle each turn.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Selesnya Allies built around airbend, using creatures that do something when they enter.
2. The Selesnya Offense counters deck from the menu (Elves, Pawpatch Recruit, Innkeeper's Talent) with airbend added in.
3. A blue-white-green version with Aang, Swift Savior, Spyglass Siren and Floodpits Drowner.

From Selesnya Offense I took only the ramp-and-pump package (4 Llanowar Elves, 3 Ouroboroid) and its 21-land mana base.

**Things to know:**
- **Fetch Quest from exile:** If Appa exiles Bramble Familiar, I expect you can cast its adventure half, Fetch Quest, from exile for {2}. That mills seven and puts a creature, enchantment or land from them onto the battlefield. I'm going by general adventure rules here, which the tools couldn't confirm, so check it with a judge.
- **Mana:** The check flagged 18 green sources against about 21.7 in Selesnya Offense lists, so I raised it to 19 with a 21st land. That still runs green a bit lighter than those lists to make room for 16 white sources for Appa's {W}{W}.
- **Consistency:** With 4 copies, Airbender Ascension won't show up early every game. The deck still works without it as a token deck with Appa recasts.
- **Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in the current results. Seam Rip and Get Lost handle Izzet and Boros aggro creatures. Heritage Reclamation and Scavenging Ooze hit graveyards and artifacts like Agatha's Soul Cauldron. Aven Interrupter and Snakeskin Veil help against Dimir Midrange.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
I built an Izzet (blue-red) Lessons Tempo deck, and it passed the deck check. It's a brew: these three spells have shown up in just one recent list, a Mono-Red deck.

**The three directions I considered**
1. **Mono-Red.** That one list already runs all three spells, with Fire Nation Cadets, Firebending Student and Hired Claw. Copying it wouldn't be a brew, and it doesn't use the blue half of Abandon Attachments.
2. **Temur (blue-red-green), built around Iroh, Grand Lotus.** On your turn, Iroh gives every Lesson in your graveyard flashback for {1}, and Hermitic Herbalist adds mana for Lessons. It's powerful, but it needs a 6-mana creature and a three-color mana base.
3. **Izzet Lessons Tempo (chosen).** It takes the blue-red land package from the Vivi Cauldron menu deck (Riverpyre Verge, Spirebluff Canal, Thundering Falls) and Burst Lightning from Izzet Aggro. Everything else is built around your three cards. I picked it because blue has the most cards that grow stronger for each Lesson in your graveyard, so every spell you cast also improves your creatures.

**The plan**
Play cheap creatures that grow when you cast Lessons:
- **Sokka:** gets a +1/+1 counter whenever you cast a Lesson.
- **First-Time Flyer:** a 2-mana flyer that gets +1/+1 once a Lesson is in your graveyard.
- **Stormcatch Mentor:** makes your instants and sorceries cost 1 less.
- **Dragonfly Swarm:** a flyer whose power equals the number of noncreature, nonland cards in your graveyard.

Firebending Lesson, Burst Lightning and Iroh's Demonstration clear blockers early. Abandon Attachments trades away extra lands for new cards and puts another Lesson in the graveyard. That pile powers up Combustion Technique, which deals 2 damage plus 1 for each Lesson in your graveyard and exiles what it kills. It also pays off Accumulate Wisdom, which puts all three cards it looks at into your hand once you have three Lessons in the graveyard. Late in the game, Serpent of the Pass costs 1 less for each noncreature, nonland card in your graveyard, and with three Lessons there you can cast it at instant speed.

**Numbers**
- There are 17 Lessons in the main deck. On the play, you have a 94% chance of seeing one by turn 2 and an 85% chance of seeing a 2-mana creature.
- I'm running 21 lands. The checker recommended about 23, but the average mana value is 2.15, nothing costs more than 3 except the cheaper-than-printed Serpent, and Abandon Attachments turns extra lands into new cards.
- About 37% of the deck matches an existing Vivi Cauldron list, well under the brew limit.

**Sideboard**
Each group is aimed at specific decks from the menu:
- **Aggro decks (Izzet, Boros, Simic):** 2 more Iroh's Demonstration and 2 Fire Magic.
- **Dimir, Jeskai and Azorius Control:** 2 Spell Pierce, 2 Negate, 2 Disdainful Stroke and 1 It'll Quench Ya!, a counterspell that's also a Lesson.
- **Vivi Cauldron and Reanimator:** 2 Abrade for Agatha's Soul Cauldron and 2 Soul-Guide Lantern for graveyards.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built an Izzet (blue-red) Elementals tempo-ramp deck. It's a brew, and the deck checker found it legal with no warnings.

**The plan:** Every creature in the deck is an Elemental, so Sunderflock's "return all non-Elemental creatures to their owners' hands" clears only your opponent's board. Sunderflock costs less based on the highest mana value among your Elementals:
- With a 4-drop out (Twinflame Travelers or Champion of the Path), it costs 5.
- With Shinestriker out, it costs 3.

Ashling and Flamebraider get you there early. Once Ashling transforms, she adds two mana each turn for spells costing 4 or more. Twinflame Travelers makes that trigger happen twice, so you get four mana. Bounce Off is a 1-mana tempo spell that removes blockers and stalls threats. It can also return your own Sunderflock to your hand so you can cast it again and bounce their board a second time (the bounce only happens when it's cast).

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Izzet Elementals, using the mana base from Izzet Aggro on the menu.** I took its lands (Riverpyre Verge, Spirebluff Canal) and its Burst Lightning removal, and added Steam Vents.
2. **Simic Ouroboroid with a red splash.** That deck already runs Bounce Off, but Sunderflock would bounce your own Ouroboroid and Badgermole Cubs.
3. **Izzet spells/Prowess with Stormchaser's Talent.** Almost none of its creatures are Elementals, so Sunderflock would be expensive and would bounce your own board.

I chose direction 1 because it's the only one where all three of your cards help each other.

**Key choices:**
- **Ramp:** 4 Ashling and 4 Flamebraider. Flamebraider's two mana can only be spent on Elementals, and that includes Sunderflock.
- **Finding pieces:** Eclipsed Flamekin and Flaring Cinder dig for Elementals or lands.
- **Removal:** Rimekin Recluse and Burst Lightning, plus Bounce Off.
- **Cavern of Souls (set to Elemental):** protects Sunderflock from counterspells in No More Lies decks.
- **Four copies of Ashling:** she's legendary, so you can't keep two in play. A spare copy isn't wasted, though: her enter trigger lets you discard it to draw a new card.

**Odds:** Draw odds without mulligans, on the play, by turn 4:
- 79% to have drawn Ashling or Flamebraider.
- About 53% to have drawn Sunderflock.
- About 41% to have both.

**Mana:** I ran 23 lands; the checker suggested 24. I went one lower because Ashling and Flamebraider make extra mana.

**Sideboard:**
- Counterspells for Jeskai and Lessons.
- Soul-Guide Lantern for Reanimator.
- Abrade and Explosive Prodigy for the green creature decks.
- Mouth of the Storm and Ashling's Command for aggro and decks that flood the board with small creatures.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I built a mono-black Demons deck (a brew). It ramps into Doomsday Excruciator, leaves both players with six cards in their library, and then finishes the opponent with Insatiable Avarice. Archenemy's Charm protects the plan.

**How it wins:** Casting Excruciator leaves each library with only its bottom six cards. Insatiable Avarice's {B}{B} mode makes a target player draw three cards and lose 3 life. Aim it at the opponent and two copies empty their library. Bloodletter of Aclazotz makes opponents lose twice as much life on your turn, so each Avarice also drains 6. Archenemy's Charm removes a threat, returns a dead Excruciator or Bloodletter from your graveyard, or grows a Demon and gives it lifelink.

**Watch your own library:** Excruciator also makes you draw an extra card each upkeep, so after it lands you run out of cards before the opponent does. Use Avarice on them right away; don't sit back and wait.

**Finding Excruciator:** On five mana, casting Avarice with both modes puts any card on top of your library and then draws it with two others, so it works as a tutor. Counting Avarice as a way to find Excruciator, you have an 85.3% chance to see one of the 8 by turn 6 on the play, not counting mulligans.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-Black Demons:** borrows the Mono-Black package from the tournament results (Bloodletter, Unholy Annex, cheap removal, Swamps plus Realm of Koh).
2. **Dimir Doomsday control:** adds blue counterspells to protect Excruciator.
3. **Forced-draw deck:** uses Scrawling Crawler and Avarice to empty the opponent's library.

I chose mono-black because Excruciator's {B}{B}{B}{B}{B}{B} cost rules out a real second color. The Demon theme also helps directly: Desecration Demon, Bloodletter and Excruciator are all Demons, so Unholy Annex drains 2 every turn.

**Mana and sideboard:**
- 24 lands, 23 of which make black mana, plus three copies of The Soul Stone so you can cast Excruciator on turn 5. That's in line with real Mono-Black lists, which average 24 lands and about 21 black sources.
- One Deathmark is in the main deck because the two biggest decks right now, Simic Ouroboroid and Landfall, are green.
- The sideboard targets those green decks, the aggro decks, and Reanimator.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I built a Rakdos (black-red) discard aggro deck and submitted it as a brew. The three cards fit together well. Iron-Shield Elf (3/1 for two mana) lets you discard a card to make it indestructible. Bloodthorn Flail is a one-mana equipment that gives +2/+1, and you can equip it by discarding a card instead of paying {3}. Both discards can put Flamewake Phoenix in your graveyard. The Phoenix comes back at the start of your combat if you control a creature with 4 or more power and pay {R}. Elf plus Flail is a 5/2, so it turns that on by itself.

**The plan:** Play cheap threats, discard Phoenixes and cards that can be recast from the graveyard, and attack every turn. Many creatures already have 4+ power, so Phoenix keeps returning:
- **Power-4+ creatures that bring Phoenix back:** Sunset Saboteur (4/1 menace for two) and Ultimate Green Goblin (5/4 for three).
- **Free discards:** Ultimate Green Goblin makes you discard a card every upkeep and gives you a Treasure, which can pay the {R} to bring Phoenix back. Fear of Missing Out and Bitter Triumph also let you discard.
- **Discard payoffs:** Hobgoblin gets +2/+0 each time you discard, and Marauding Mako grows a +1/+1 counter. If you discard Scarlet Spider, Kaine, you can cast it from your graveyard that turn for {B/R}.
- **Removal:** Burst Lightning and Shock, borrowed from Boros Aggro, plus Bitter Triumph.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Rakdos discard aggro (the one I chose)
2. A Boros Aggro shell built around Hired Claw and Burst Lightning, adding black
3. A Jund version using Llanowar Elves and Badgermole Cub

I chose Rakdos because every discard feeds the Phoenix and powers up another card. Both other options would have added cards that do nothing with the three you asked for.

**Mana and odds:**
- 22 lands, with 17 sources each of black and red. That's 4 Blood Crypt, 4 Blazemire Verge, 4 Haunted Ridge, 5 Swamp and 5 Mountain.
- By turn 4 on the play, you have a 98.9% chance to have a discard card or a power enabler.
- You only have a 52.8% chance to have drawn a Phoenix by then. The deck doesn't need it every game; it's a strong bonus when it shows up.

**Sideboard (15 cards), aimed at the top decks:**
- **Fell, Abrade and Fire Magic:** against creature decks like Simic Ouroboroid, Landfall, Golgari Midrange and other creature-heavy aggro.
- **Feed the Swarm:** kills the Talent enchantments in the Lessons deck.
- **Soul-Guide Lantern:** against Reanimator.
- **Duress and Thought-Stalker Warlock:** against Jeskai Control and Dimir Midrange.

Check_deck says 50% of this deck matches one recent Rogue list, which is under the 65% limit for a brew.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built a four-color (blue, red, white, black) Lute control deck as a brew. Resonating Lute makes every land tap for two mana of any one color, but only for instants and sorceries. That solves the problem of casting a red-white-black spell (Inevitable Defeat) and a 7-mana blue-red-white spell (Jeskai Revelation) in one deck. Turn 4 Lute means Revelation on turn 5, and late in the game it also turns Syncopate into a hard counter. The plan is to survive with cheap removal (Get Lost, Lightning Helix, Abrade, Day of Judgment), then cast Inevitable Defeat, Jeskai Revelation and the flashback half of Fire Nation Attacks with the doubled mana. Stock Up, Consult the Star Charts and Winternight Stories keep your hand at seven cards so Lute can also draw.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Four-color control (chosen):** uses the interaction and mana base from Jeskai Control (the menu's list with 3 Jeskai Revelation), plus a light black splash for Inevitable Defeat.
2. **Grixis (blue-black-red) draw-heavy deck:** uses the card-draw package from Dimir Excruciator. That deck's engine is a creature, which Lute's mana can't pay for, and Grixis can't cast Revelation's white or Defeat's white anyway.
3. **Jeskai Monk-token spells deck, Lessons-style:** aggressive spells deck. It wastes Lute's ramp and drops black, so Inevitable Defeat goes.

I chose direction 1 because it's the only one where all three of your cards work together: Lute fixes and ramps the two expensive multicolor instants.

**The deck:**
- **Requested cards:** a full playset of each.
- **Instant-only mana:** 2 Great Hall of the Biblioplex make any color for instants and sorceries.
- **Black for Inevitable Defeat:** 8 sources (6 lands that make black, plus the 2 Great Halls). Once Lute is out, any land works.
- **Mana base:** 25 lands. The check tool's recommendation was 24.9; real Jeskai Control lists run about 26. I went slightly lower because Lute does some of the ramping.

**Things to know:**
- **Your odds:** you have about a 57% chance to see a Lute by turn 5 on the play, not counting digging. Stock Up and Consult push that higher, but some games you'll have to play fair control without it.
- **Why it isn't just Jeskai Control:** the first draft matched an existing four-color Inevitable Defeat list too closely (68%). So I cut No More Lies and most of the Consult the Star Charts copies. In their place I put Syncopate, Winternight Stories (its harmonize cost from the graveyard can be paid with Lute's mana) and Fire Nation Attacks. The final list is 58% one existing list, under the 65% brew limit.
- **Sideboard:** Pyroclasm, Requiting Hex, Seam Rip and Spell Snare are for the aggressive decks (Prowess, Landfall, Aang). Negate and Disdainful Stroke are for the slower spell decks. Tishana's Tidebinder and Ultima cover the rest.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:

**The plan:** Play a 1- or 2-mana Dwarf every turn and equip it cheaply.
- **Card flow:** Dáin's Company looks at the top four cards for a Dwarf or Equipment. Kíli draws a card when another Dwarf or Equipment enters (once a turn). Giott lets you discard a card to draw one when they enter.
- **Free equips:** Kíli's equip discount only works with "storied," meaning three or more artifacts or legendary cards in play. Lots of the deck counts toward that: Kíli, Giott, Thorin, Dáin, Fíli, Lost Jitte, Mjölnir and every Equipment. Once you have it, your first equip each turn costs nothing.
- **Mauler:** equips aimed at it cost 2 less, so most cost nothing.
- **Damage:** Giott has double strike, and Dáin Ironfoot gives every equipped attacker double strike. Mjölnir doubles all damage the equipped creature deals, so these stack fast. Mjölnir's entry also deals 4 damage to a creature.
- **Removal:** 4 Burst Lightning and 1 Lightning Helix.

**Numbers:**

- 22 lands is below the 23.4 that Boros Aggro averages. That's on purpose: the deck's average mana value is only 1.92.

**Sideboard (15):** aimed at the top decks on the menu.
- **Prowess and Lessons:** Magebane Lizard punishes their noncreature spells. Sear and Scorching Shot kill Eddymurk Crab and other big creatures.
- **Graveyard decks:** Ghost Vacuum for Reanimator and Dimir Excruciator.
- **Artifacts:** Abrade for Brightglass Gearhulk and other artifact threats.
- **Control:** Dawn's Truce protects your board against 4C Control's removal and its Day of Judgment sweepers.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built this as **Rakdos Treasure Aristocrats**, a brew for Standard. The deck is mostly black, with a light red splash.

**The plan:** Greedy Freebooter, Common Crook and Bloodghast are creatures you're happy to sacrifice. Freebooter and Crook leave a Treasure when they die, and Bloodghast comes back from the graveyard whenever you play a land.
- **Umbral Collar Zealot** is a free sacrifice outlet you can use any time: each sacrifice lets you surveil 1 (look at the top card and choose whether to put it in the graveyard).
- **The Sackville-Bagginses** turns one sacrifice into a card plus a Treasure. It also makes your opponent lose 1 life every time you sacrifice a token, and that includes every Treasure you spend for mana.
- **Sephiroth, Popular Egotist and Venerated Stormsinger** add more drains on top. Each of them makes the opponent lose 1 life (and you gain 1) whenever your creatures die or you sacrifice something.
- **Totentanz** makes a Rat token whenever one of your nontoken creatures dies, so you always have more to sacrifice.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-black aristocrats:** the cleanest mana.
2. **Golgari Food:** built around Scavenger's Talent, Experimental Confectioner and the Golgari Roots shell.
3. **Rakdos, borrowing from Mardu Discard:** take Mardu Discard's Bloodghast plus its black-red lands (Blood Crypt and Blazemire Verge).

I chose the Rakdos version. It keeps the black core and adds Totentanz as more fodder, plus Burst Lightning as cheap removal against Prowess, the biggest deck in the field at 17%.

**The numbers:**
- check_deck found no errors. It's 36.7% the same as the closest Mardu Discard list, well under the 65% limit for a brew.
- Its one note was that Mardu Discard lists run about 15 white sources and this has 2. That doesn't matter, because this deck has no white cards.
- I run 23 lands instead of the donor's roughly 22 because Bloodghast wants a land drop every turn. The average card costs only about 2 mana, so Treasures make up for any extra lands.
- With 12 sacrifice outlets and 11 cheap fodder creatures, you'll see at least one outlet by turn 3 about 89% of the time. The odds of having both an outlet and a fodder creature by then are about 76%.

**Sideboard:**
- **Duress and Strategic Betrayal** are for Lessons, control and Dimir Excruciator.
- **Shock, Abrade and Shoot the Sheriff** are extra removal for Prowess, Landfall and Selesnya Offense.
- **Magic Pot** exiles cards from graveyards against Reanimator, and leaves a Treasure when it dies.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Sentinel of the Nameless City, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder.
results.text:
I built **Golgari Explore Midrange**, a brew. It's a black-green deck that takes away the opponent's best cards and answers what they play, then wins with creatures that keep growing.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Golgari explore (chosen).** Sentinel of the Nameless City makes a Map token when it enters and each time it attacks. A Map lets one of your creatures "explore," and explore creatures fit around that.
2. **Jund Fable midrange.** This would take Fable of the Mirror-Breaker and Bloodtithe Harvester from Rakdos Midrange and add green for the two removal spells. It needs three colors, though, and nothing in it works with Sentinel.
3. **Golgari Witch's Oven sacrifice**, taken from Jund Sacrifice. Neither Sentinel nor Tear Asunder does anything for that engine.

I picked the first one because it's the only plan where Sentinel matters as more than a solid 3/4 body.

**How it plays:**
- **Exploring:** When a creature explores, you reveal your top card. Fight Rigging puts a +1/+1 counter on it at the start of your combat, which makes it 7 power. The deck is packed with good cards to hide: Turntimber Symbiosis, Emrakul, the Promised End, both Ghaltas and Trumpeting Carnosaur. results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Apex Devastator, Call Forth the Tempest and Creative Technique.
results.text:

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Cloudpost lands.** Cloudpost, Glimmerpost and Planar Nexus ramp without adding spells, so Technique flips fewer bad cards. But Cloudpost enters tapped, so 5 mana usually arrives on turn 3 at the earliest, and it makes only colorless mana.

I chose the third because it can cast Technique on turn 2 (Tomb + City + a Spirit Guide makes 5 mana with red). Also, casting a card "without paying its mana cost" ignores colors, so the green Apex Devastator doesn't need green mana and the deck can stay mono-red.

**The plan:** Cast Creative Technique early. It flips cards until it hits a spell and lets you cast it free:
- **Apex Devastator** gives four cascades. Those can find Call Forth the Tempest, more Techniques, Ugin or Inferno Titan.
- **Call Forth the Tempest** cascades twice more. Then it deals damage to each of the opponent's creatures equal to the mana value of everything else you cast that turn. After Technique (5) plus Apex (10), that's already at least 15.
- **Emrakul or Ulamog** can only come from Technique, not cascade, because cascade only finds cheaper spells. Emrakul gives an extra turn and Ulamog exiles two permanents.

**Backup and defense:**
- The One Ring buys time and digs for a Technique.
- Ancient Tomb mana lets you cast Ugin, Inferno Titan and eventually Call Forth normally.
- Fury and Pyroblast handle the blue tempo decks, which make up about a third of the field.

- **Odds:** With 4 Techniques, you'll have one by turn 3 on the play only about 49% of the time. You'll have fast mana about 95% of the time, and both together about 46%. Treat the other half of your games as "Ring and Titans until Technique shows up."
- **Bad flips:** About a quarter of Technique's possible hits are weak: Spirit Guide, Chrome Mox or Pyroblast.

**Sideboard:** It targets the decks currently winning: graveyard hate (Leyline of the Void, Faerie Macabre, Tormod's Crypt) for the reanimation in Esper Tempo and for Oops All Spells, extra blue counters (Pyroblast, Red Elemental Blast), Fiery Confluence for Ocelot Aggro and Cephalid Breakfast, and Disruptor Flute and Pithing Needle for the artifact combo decks (Tron and Mystic Forge) and Lands.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:

**How it wins:** Buried Alive puts three Phoenixes in your graveyard, and Buried Alive itself counts toward the three instants and sorceries Phoenix needs. A typical turn 3–4 is Buried Alive, then Lava Dart, then Lava Dart's flashback (which costs no mana: you sacrifice a Volcanic Island or Badlands, since both count as Mountains). That's three spells, and three hasty 3/2 fliers come back at the start of combat. Flow State is your card advantage: there's almost always an instant and a sorcery in your graveyard, so it usually puts two cards in your hand. Manamorphose gives back the two mana it costs and draws a card, so it adds a spell to the count for free.

**The three directions I sketched:**
1. **Grixis Phoenix tempo (chosen).** Borrows Izzet Tempo's cantrips, Force of Will, Bolt and mana base, and adds black for Buried Alive.
2. **Phoenix–Reanimator hybrid.** Buried Alive would also bin Griselbrand, with Reanimate and Animate Dead. This splits the deck between two plans that each need their own cards.
3. **Dimir-style Phoenix.** Built on Fatal Push, Thoughtseize and Bowmasters. This has fewer free and cheap spells to reach three in one turn.

I picked direction 1 because Izzet Tempo's pile of one-mana spells, plus Lava Dart and Manamorphose, is exactly what makes three spells in a turn easy.

**What I borrowed vs. added:**
- **From Izzet Tempo:** 4 Brainstorm, 4 Ponder, 4 Force of Will, 4 Lightning Bolt, 4 Dragon's Rage Channeler, Murktide Regent, and the fetch/dual-land mana. Channeler's surveil (look at the top card, optionally put it in the graveyard) can bin a Phoenix.
- **My additions:** 4 Buried Alive, 4 Flow State, 4 Lava Dart, 3 Manamorphose and 2 Faithless Looting. Looting is a second way to discard Phoenixes.
- **One Murktide:** it's a backup threat for when the opponent exiles your graveyard. Delve eats spells you've already used, not your Phoenixes.

**Honest odds:** With 4 Buried Alive and 2 Looting you have about a 64% chance to see one in your first 9 cards (on the play, by turn 3). That doesn't count Brainstorm, Ponder or Flow State digging for them, so the real number is higher.

**Mana:** 18 lands, which is a little under Izzet Tempo's average of 18.9. I'm comfortable with that because the average mana value is 2.17 and Manamorphose replaces itself. There are 9 black sources for Buried Alive and 11 red sources.

**Weak spots:** Graveyard hate like Surgical Extraction or Grafdigger's Cage hurts the deck badly. Phoenix is also weak against fast sweepers and against Orcish Bowmasters (Dimir Tempo's top creature).

**Sideboard (15)**, aimed at the current top decks:
- Pyroblast and Hydroblast for the blue and red tempo decks
- Force of Negation, Consign to Memory and Thoughtseize for Sneak and Show, Oops All Spells, Reanimator and Doomsday
- Fatal Push and Pyroclasm for Ocelot Aggro
- Meltdown for Tron and Eldrazi
- Surgical Extraction and Tormod's Crypt for graveyard decks. I left out Grafdigger's Cage because it would stop your own Phoenixes from returning.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I submitted the deck as a **UR Welder combo brew** for Vintage. Your three cards make an infinite combo, and the deck is built to assemble it.

**The combo (from the rules text):** Sewer-veillance Cam says "When this artifact enters **or leaves** the battlefield, you may tap or untap target creature." Goblin Welder taps to swap an artifact you control with an artifact card in your graveyard. Start with one of Extruder or Cam on the battlefield and the other in your graveyard:
1. Welder swaps Cam out for Extruder. Cam leaving untaps Welder, and Extruder entering deals 2 damage.
2. Welder swaps Extruder out for Cam. Cam entering untaps Welder.
3. Repeat. Every two swaps deals 2 damage, with no limit.

Welder has to have started the turn under your control, because the untap doesn't get around summoning sickness. Goblin Engineer is the backup: each swap costs {R}, and its entry trigger puts a combo piece straight from your library into your graveyard. That covers the hardest part of the setup.

**Three directions I sketched:**
- **UR combo** using the blue power-and-Force package from the menu's Lurrus PO and Paradoxical Outcome decks: Moxen, Lotus, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt, Mana Vault, Ancestral, Time Walk and Force of Will.
- **Grixis**, adding black tutors and Underground Seas from the Tinker shell.
- **Mishra's Workshop prison** with the loop as the finisher.

**I chose UR** because two colors keep a turn-1 red source reliable for Welder. Goblin Engineer, Fabricate and Thirst for Knowledge already find the pieces or put them in the graveyard, so black tutors add little. Workshop mana is colorless only, so it can't cast Legion Extruder on its own.

**Plan:** Fast mana and cheap red creatures go first. Engineer, Thirst, Faithless Looting, Dack Fayden and Extruder's own sacrifice ability get one piece into the graveyard. Force of Will, Pyroblast and Bolt protect the Welder until the loop kills.

**Things to know:**
- **Odds:** On the play with no mulligans, you have at least one Welder or Engineer plus at least one Extruder, Cam or Fabricate by turn 3 in about 58% of games. You'll also need mana and a way to fill the graveyard, so expect some games to go long. The 1 Wurmcoil Engine is a backup Welder target for those.
- **Vexing Bauble is left out on purpose.** It counters any spell cast without spending mana, which would hit your own Moxen and your free Force of Will casts.
- **One change after the check:** check_deck flagged about 11 blue and 11 red sources. I cut one Faithless Looting for a 15th land (a second Mountain, since 4 Volcanic Island is the limit), and the final deck was accepted with no warnings.
- **Sideboard:** it targets the field. Graveyard hate goes against Dredge, artifact removal against the Shops decks and Paradoxical Outcome, sweepers against Initiative, and extra red blasts and counters against the Lurrus decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:

**How it works:** Both Eidolons return from your graveyard to your hand whenever you cast a multicolored spell. 24 of the deck's 41 spells are multicolored, and you'll draw at least one by turn 4 about 99.7% of the time. That means you can sacrifice the Eidolons every turn without losing them:

Each time an Eidolon comes back, a card leaves your graveyard, so Spirit Mascot gets a +1/+1 counter. Pursue the Past fits especially well. It's a two-color spell that lets you discard an Eidolon to draw two. Casting it again with flashback brings an Eidolon back and also takes Pursue out of the graveyard, which can trigger Mascot twice.

**Directions I considered:**

2. A version using the Mono-Red Rally deck's Burning-Tree Emissary, which counts as multicolored.
3. A Boros multicolored creature deck, borrowing the Synthesizer deck's two-color lands and removal.

I chose the third because it's the only one where both Eidolons get back to your hand nearly every turn. The other two only feed Mascot.

**Borrowed from Synthesizer:** Kor Skyfisher, Lightning Bolt, Journey to Nowhere, the Wind-Scarred Crag / Boros Garrison land base, and most of the sideboard. The checker found the deck is 41.7% the same as one Synthesizer list (the limit for a brew is 65%).

**Mana:** I run 19 lands, with 13 red and 13 white sources. That's below Synthesizer's average of 20.5 but above the checker's suggested 17.7. The extra lands are there to pay for the 4-mana Eidolons, Pursue's 4-mana flashback and the sacrifice costs.

**Honest odds:** You'll have an Eidolon by turn 4 only about 68% of the time, and Spirit Mascot about 53%. The deck still works as a cheap, efficient aggro deck when those cards don't show up.

**The three directions I considered**
1. **Black-Green with Hermit Druid and Survival (chosen).** It borrows two packages from the menu: Hermit Druid, Survival of the Fittest and Birds of Paradise from Hermit Druid Combo, and the Cabal Therapy/Duress hand attack. Living Death has already shown up in 3 recent BG Survival lists.
2. **Mono-black with Dark Ritual and Buried Alive.** It would use Reanimator's Putrid Imp, Lotus Petal and Ritual.
3. **Blue-Black self-mill.** Careful Study and card-draw spells to discard creatures.

I picked the first because green gives you four different ways to fill the graveyard. Hermit Druid, Survival, Buried Alive and Krosan Tusker's cycling all do it, plus Birds to reach 5 mana. The other two directions rely on a narrower set of discard outlets.

**How it plays**
- **Filling the graveyard:**
  - **Hermit Druid:** The deck runs only 9 basic lands, so each activation mills a big chunk of the library.
  - **Survival of the Fittest:** Discard a creature to search for another.
  - **Buried Alive:** Puts three creatures straight into the graveyard.
  - **Krosan Tusker:** Cycling it draws a card and finds a basic land, and leaves a 6/5 in the graveyard.
- **What comes back:**
  - Visara and Bone Shredder kill creatures when they return.
  - Deranged Hermit brings four squirrels.
  - Akroma and Phantom Nishoba are strong against red decks.
  - Symbiotic Wurm makes seven insects whenever it dies, including when a second Living Death sacrifices it.
  - Akroma and Nishoba can't realistically be cast from hand. They're only there to come back from the graveyard, which is why I ignored the deck checker's warning about having only 7 white sources.
- **Finding and protecting Living Death:**
  - Diabolic Intent can search for it. Sacrifice a Druid or Bird you've already used.
  - Dark Ritual can make a turn-3 Living Death possible.
  - Therapy and Duress clear counterspells out of the way first, which matters most against Stiflenought.

**Honest odds:** Without a mulligan, you have about a 61% chance of holding Living Death or a Diabolic Intent by turn 4. You'll almost always have a way to fill the graveyard by then (about 96%), so the real bottleneck is drawing Living Death itself.

**Things to watch for**
- Living Death also brings back creatures in the opponent's graveyard.
- The pain lands (Llanowar Wastes, City of Brass) cost life against Sligh.
- The deck runs 20 lands, slightly below the roughly 21 that BG Survival lists play. Birds, Dark Ritual and Tusker's land search make up the difference.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks:
- Engineered Plague for Goblins and Elves
- Smother for Dreadnought and small creatures
- Xantid Swarm against counterspell decks
- Naturalize and Pernicious Deed for Enchantress and Oath
- Tormod's Crypt for opposing graveyard decks
- Uktabi Orangutan to destroy artifacts (Survival can fetch it)
- A spare Duress
